intro: PowerPoint for financial analysts on Mac means three jobs: turning Excel tables into charts, keeping one slide master, and updating numbers without rebuilding the deck. The Mac version handles all three, but its menus differ from Windows and linked Excel charts need a manual refresh.
tldr: Turn each Excel range into one clean table before you insert a chart with Insert > Chart.
Mac PowerPoint does not prompt to update linked Excel charts, so run Chart Design > Refresh Data before every send.
Set size and orientation once with Slide Master > Slide Size > Page Setup, then save the master as a template.
Check your Office license before a deadline. Microsoft says some macOS users may enter reduced functionality mode from July 13, 2026.

blocks.text: What finance analysts build in PowerPoint on Mac

Most finance decks are not one-off presentations. They are recurring pages that get reviewed, marked up and reissued each cycle. MCell's guide to financial slides names budget variance, profit bridge, cash flow and revenue mix as slide types for FP&A reviews, CFO updates and board packs. MCell is a vendor, so treat its advice as a starting point, not a rulebook.

The time cost is real. A UpSlide and CSA study of 178 banking, financial and insurance professionals reports that 90% spend at least 2 hours a day in PowerPoint. The article does not describe recruitment or questions, so treat the figure as a signal, not a benchmark.
Start from one clean Excel table

The fastest way to a clean chart starts in Excel, before you touch PowerPoint. MCell recommends one clean table for each chart, with row names, units and order fixed. Build it that way and the chart needs fewer fixes later.
Use this order for each chart:

items: Put units in the row or column header, not inside the numbers.
Sort the rows the way the slide reads, top to bottom or left to right.
Delete helper columns and totals you do not plan to chart.
Name the sheet and range so you can find them when the numbers change.
Copy the range with ⌘C, switch to PowerPoint, and paste it into the chart's data sheet with ⌘V.

blocks.text: Stable structure matters more than the first chart. MCell notes that native PowerPoint charts become fragile when numbers, groupings or scenarios change. For a recurring deck, keep the same rows in the same order every month.
Pick chart types that match the question

Microsoft's financial presentation templates page gives a simple rule. Use line charts for trends, pie charts for proportions and bar charts for comparisons. The table below applies that rule to the questions finance reviewers ask.

rows: Is a number moving over time?
Monthly cash balance across a quarter
Which cost centers are over plan?
What share does each segment hold?
Revenue mix with a handful of segments
How did profit get from last year to this year?
Profit bridge with one bar per driver
blocks.caption: Chart types for common finance review questions.

blocks.text: A pie chart earns its place only with a few slices and one question. If a reviewer asks for a pie with many slices, a sorted bar chart with the same numbers reads faster. Offer both, and let the reviewer choose.
Why Excel charts go stale on Mac

This is the Mac limit that matters most for recurring decks. In a 2017 Microsoft Q&A thread, a Microsoft representative said Mac PowerPoint 2016 cannot update the source path of linked or embedded Excel charts. The Windows Edit Links to Files option has no Mac equivalent, and the recommended workaround is Chart Design > Refresh Data.

A user in the same thread reported that Mac PowerPoint does not prompt to update linked chart data when a file opens, unlike Windows. The chart keeps the old numbers until someone refreshes it. The thread is from 2017, so test the behavior in your version before you rely on it.
Refreshing a chart is simple once you know where it lives. Click the chart first. The Chart Design tab appears only when a chart is selected. Then choose Chart Design > Refresh Data.
Refresh routine before every send

items: Open the source workbook and confirm the final numbers.
Click the chart in PowerPoint and check that the Chart Design tab appears.
Choose Chart Design > Refresh Data.
Compare the total, the largest bar and the last period with the workbook.
Save a PDF for reviewers, and keep the editable file for yourself.

blocks.text: Write the refresh step into your close checklist. Skipping it is how an old number reaches a review meeting.

blocks.title: Check your license first
blocks.text: Microsoft's known-issues page and release notes do not fully agree on Office 2021 for Mac. Check the license status inside the app before you promise a file by a set date.
Choose how each chart is pasted or embedded

Paste options change what happens later. A picture cannot be refreshed or edited as data. An embedded chart carries its own data sheet inside the file, so it works offline but does not follow the workbook. A linked chart points back to the workbook, which is where the Mac refresh problem appears.
For recurring decks, use charts with a documented refresh step, and keep the workbook next to the deck. For a one-time exhibit, a picture is fine once the numbers are final.
Set up the slide master once on Mac

A slide master sets fonts, colors, logo position and page layouts for the whole file. A finance deck built on a master can be reissued with new numbers and still look consistent. The Mac menus differ from Windows, so use these paths.

items: Open the master with View > Slide Master.
Set orientation and size with Slide Master > Slide Size > Page Setup. Windows uses Custom Slide Size for this job.
Add a second master with Insert Slide Master on the Slide Master tab, for example one for board packs and one for internal reviews.
Save the finished file as a template with File > Save as Template.

blocks.text: Microsoft's slide master guide covers the basics on Mac. Its theme guidance is brief, and it points to a separate theme article. Read both before you build a company theme.

blocks.title: Set the master first
blocks.text: Changing the theme after every slide is built costs more time than setting it first. Build the master, then add the charts.
Save a clean master before anyone edits a client or team copy. MCell recommends the same step, because a clean master gives every later edit a known starting point.
Build a profit bridge step by step

A profit bridge shows how you got from one profit figure to another. Start with last period's operating profit as the first bar. Add one bar for each driver, such as price, volume and cost. Each driver bar goes up when profit rose and down when it fell. End with this period's operating profit.

In Excel, build a small table with one row per driver. Keep the sign convention fixed. Positive means profit rose, and negative means it fell. Then chart the table as stacked columns, color the start and end bars alike, and let the driver bars float between them.

Two edge cases trip people up. A driver that changes sign between versions flips its bar color, so check the color after every refresh. A rounding gap between the bridge total and the reported figure shows on the slide, so decide on decimals before you start.
Finish with the MCell checklist. Remove gridlines, drop redundant legends and add direct labels on each bar. Those three changes let a reviewer read the bridge without help.
Build a monthly budget variance slide

A budget variance slide compares actual against budget by line item. Use a bar chart with one bar per cost center, or a table with color only on the variance column. Put the question in the title, such as 'Which departments are over plan this month?'

Keep the same row order every month. A reviewer who sees Marketing in row four last month expects it there again. Changing the order makes a recurring deck harder to read, and it makes the refresh step riskier.
Mistakes that waste a finance analyst's afternoon

items: Pasting a chart as a picture, then finding out the numbers changed.
Leaving gridlines, a legend and a repeated title in place. Each one adds reading time.
Rebuilding the same deck from scratch each month instead of saving a master.
Starting from a canned template with different fonts and colors. Indezine's 2004 survey found 61% of people who use canned templates sometimes or always redo them.
Spending too long on content. The same survey found 58% of professionals spend more than three hours for each 30-minute talk deciding what goes in.

blocks.text: Those survey numbers are old, and the sample was self-selected and not finance-specific. Use them as a warning about habits, not as a benchmark for your team.
What changed in PowerPoint for Mac lately

Microsoft's release notes list recent PowerPoint for Mac builds. Version 16.109 arrived on May 12, 2026 with Copilot editing, which lets you create, edit and refine presentations in natural language. Version 16.107 arrived on March 10, 2026 and stopped saving a PNG fallback for SVG graphics in .pptx files.

Copilot features depend on your Microsoft 365 Copilot license. The notes list brand-kit template application and brand-compliance checks under Microsoft 365 Copilot Premium, so check your tier before you plan around them.

The newest build I could verify is 16.114.3, build 26102720, dated Oct 27, 2026. Microsoft describes it as quality and performance improvements only. Check Help > Check for Updates to see what your Mac runs.
For SVG logos, test the deck in the oldest app your reviewers use. Without a PNG fallback, an older viewer may not show the logo the way you expect.
Check your Office license before a deadline

Microsoft's known-issues page says that starting July 13, 2026, some Microsoft 365 subscribers on macOS, and users of non-subscription Office 2021 or 2019 on macOS, may enter reduced functionality mode. In that mode PowerPoint can open and print, but it cannot edit, save or create files.

The release notes still list Office 2021 updates in late October 2026, so the two sources do not yet agree. Check your license inside the app, and treat either source as current only after you confirm it.
Office 2019 for Mac reached end of support on October 10, 2023 and no longer receives updates. If your team still runs it, plan the upgrade before your next quarterly cycle.
Where Lazur fits in a finance deck session

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. Hold ⌥ ⌘ (Option and Command) to ask about anything on screen, and Lazur answers out loud. Ask where something is and it draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something and it guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.
Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. You make every change to the chart, the master and the numbers. Lazur points, explains and types text when you ask it to.

Dictation helps with the writing around a deck. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots cover the footnotes and company names you type every cycle.

Privacy matters with confidential figures. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Check your firm's rules before you share unreleased results with any AI tool.

Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for PowerPoint, and it has no partnership with any app maker. [Pricing and the trial](/pricing) are on their own page, and [the PowerPoint page](/apps/powerpoint) covers voice help in slides.
A checklist before you send the deck

items: Refresh every linked chart with Chart Design > Refresh Data.
Check three numbers against the workbook: the total, the largest bar and the last period.
Remove gridlines, redundant legends and extra colors.
Confirm size and orientation under Slide Master > Slide Size > Page Setup.
Save a PDF for reviewers and keep the editable file for yourself.
Save a clean master with File > Save as Template if the deck repeats next month.

blocks.text: Name files with the date and version, such as Board_Pack_v3_2026-11-08.pptx. A dated name helps a reviewer find the right copy in a thread full of attachments.
Next steps for your next close

Start with the chart you rebuild most. Clean its table, pick the right chart type and save the slide as part of a master. Then repeat the process for the next page. Keep your checklist next to the file, so the steps stay the same each cycle.

For the workbook side of the same job, read [Excel for financial analysts on Mac](/for/financial-analysts/excel). If you want voice help while you work, [download Lazur](/download) and test the shortcut on a real slide.

faq.question: Does PowerPoint for Mac update linked Excel charts automatically?
faq.answer: Not reliably. A 2017 Microsoft Q&A thread reported that Mac PowerPoint does not prompt to update linked chart data when a file opens. Select the chart and choose Chart Design > Refresh Data before each send, then test the behavior in your current build.

faq.question: Where is slide size on PowerPoint for Mac?
faq.answer: Open View > Slide Master, then choose Slide Master > Slide Size > Page Setup. Windows uses Custom Slide Size for the same job, so Windows instructions will not match your menus.

faq.question: Can I use PowerPoint for Mac without a Microsoft 365 subscription?
faq.answer: It depends on your license. Microsoft says that from July 13, 2026, some users of non-subscription Office 2021 or 2019 on macOS may enter reduced functionality mode, where PowerPoint cannot edit, save or create files. Check your status inside the app.

faq.question: Does Lazur edit my slides or charts for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur guides, points, explains and types text when you ask. It does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps. You make every change yourself, so the numbers stay under your control.

faq.question: Is financial data sent to AI providers when I use Lazur?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Check your firm's rules before you share unreleased results with any AI tool.

faq.question: Which PowerPoint for Mac version is current?
faq.answer: Microsoft's release notes list PowerPoint for Mac 16.114.3, build 26102720, dated Oct 27, 2026, as a quality and performance update. Newer builds may exist after that date, so check Help > Check for Updates.
